request: So I want a belt idler. The housing takes a 6 mm wide GT2 belt (1.38 mm thick, smooth back to the bearings) and the whole thing must print as one FDM part with no supports, and be no bigger than 40 x 40 x 25 mm. Inside there are two 623 bearings (3 x 10 x 4 mm) on top of each other on one M3 x 12 bolt, acting as a roller; their outer rings must spin freely with at least 0.4 mm of air all round, in a chamber no wider than 12 mm. The bolt head presses on the upper bearing and a small boss rising from the floor (4.6 to 5.0 mm across, 0.3 to 0.8 mm tall, not touching the outer ring) holds up the lower one, so both inner rings are clamped. Underneath the floor there is a hex pocket trapping an M3 nut (5.7 to 5.9 mm across flats, 2.6 to 3.4 mm deep, leaving at least 1.2 mm of floor over it); the bolt must reach at least 1.5 mm into that nut. You drop the bearings and bolt in from the top and the nut from the bottom. The belt goes straight through on one side of the roller, standing on its edge so its width is along the bolt axis, and its back must just touch both bearings: within 0.3 mm, at least 2 mm of overlap on each, centred on the stack within 0.25 mm. Cut a 7 mm wide belt channel, so the belt has 0.5 mm spare each side and at least 0.5 mm on the tooth side. To tension the belt you slide the block along it, so add a single slot for an M3 screw into the machine frame: 5 mm of travel, 3.3 to 3.6 mm wide, with space for the screw head and a hex key anywhere along the travel. Requirements: From the parts catalogue, put in the belt run, the two 623 bearings, the M3 bolt, the M3 nut and the M3 mounting screw. Stack the bearings on the bolt on a common axis, running across the width of the belt, and declare this layout. Bearings rest directly against each other, held between the bolt head and a boss on the floor (4.6 to 5.0 mm across, 0.3 to 0.8 mm high) which touches nothing but the inner ring of the lower bearing; the bolt passes through the floor without touching. Outer rings must be free to turn, with 0.4 mm or more between them and the block on every side, inside a chamber not wider than 12 mm. Bearings and bolt go in from the top, the nut from the bottom, all without touching the block. Channel for the belt: 7 mm wide, straight through and open at each end of the block, leaving 0.5 mm beside the belt on both sides and 0.5 mm or more on the tooth side. The belt's smooth back must just touch the outer rings of both bearings, not pushed into them (gap between 0 and 0.3 mm). It overlaps each bearing's width by 2 mm or more, and is centred on the stack to within 0.25 mm. Provide one slot, 3.3 to 3.6 mm wide, so the block can travel 5 mm along the belt on an M3 mounting screw; the head and a hex key must have room along the full travel. A hex pocket under the floor, opening onto the mounting face, holds the nut: 5.7 to 5.9 mm across flats and 2.6 to 3.4 mm deep, with 1.2 mm or more of floor over it. The bolt tip is at least 1.5 mm inside the nut and stays inside the block. The block must be a single manifold body that FDM prints without supports; every wall at least 2 mm thick. Overall dimensions no more than 40 x 40 x 25 mm, and the block sits flat on its mounting face. Hand over the block STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's clearance report, which has to agree with an independent measurement.
